articles.title: Do Companies That Stack the Vote Do Worse?
articles.mainIdea: Do Companies That Stack the Vote Do Worse?
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal: Do Companies That Stack the Vote Do Worse?. Allbirds wasn’t just the unofficial footwear provider of Silicon Valley—its initial public offering in 2021 tapped into the tech sector’s ethos by giving the company’s founders disproportionate sway in how it would be run. Salad chain Sweetgreen eyewear seller Warby Parker language-learning app Duolingo and social network Snap all have share classes with extra votes for founders and each has incinerated billions in shareholder wealth recently. The structure had a revival last year with companies like Klarna, Figma and StubHub. Related tickers mentioned: BIRD, BRK-B, DDS, META, WRBY.
